lead_independence.lead: Kelsey Weidenheimer, a neighbor on Southwest Alligator Street, said she and others had been calling the Martin County Sheriff's Office about the dogs since 2020. She said when she called, she told them the dogs were kept inside the house, had not been let out in years, and that there was no air conditioning because the windows were open. source_focus.source_title: Border Collies begin recovery after Palm City hoarding case; owner faces 72 cruelty counts - cw34.com
source_focus.source_lead: The Border Collies rescued from a Palm City home Monday where authorities found deplorable conditions are now receiving medical care, nourishment and grooming as they begin their recovery. The Humane Society of the Treasure Coast said it has taken in the dogs rescued by the Martin County Sheriff's Office Animal Services Unit and is assessing their needs while determining the best path forward.

article_framing_rejections.headline: Humane Society seeks donations after Martin County hoarding cases deplete emergency fund

lead_independence.headline: Humane Society seeks donations after Martin County hoarding cases deplete emergency fund
lead_independence.lead: Sarah Fisher, a spokeswoman for the Humane Society of the Treasure Coast in Palm City, said the biggest need is monetary donations to the emergency medical fund. The shelter took in more than 100 animals from an alleged hoarder in July, followed by 36 Border Collies rescued Monday from a Palm City home. Fisher said the cases are depleting the emergency medical fund.

source_focus.source_title: 36 dogs, 72 charges: Martin County woman accused of animal cruelty; rescued dogs begin long recovery - WPBF
source_focus.source_lead: A Palm City woman is in custody on a $270,000 bond after authorities discovered 36 Border Collies living in severe neglect inside her home on Alligator Street, leading to 72 charges of animal cruelty. Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek said the animals were in "deplorable conditions." The case dates back to 2020, when animal services first investigated Paige O'Donnell’s home and dogs.

source_focus.source_title: 'Deplorable conditions': Martin County woman accused of hoarding 36 dogs - WPBF
source_focus.source_lead: A Martin County woman is facing felony and misdemeanor animal cruelty charges after deputies discovered 36 dogs living in unsanitary conditions inside her Palm City home. The Martin County Sheriff’s Office executed a search warrant earlier today and spent much of the afternoon removing the animals, which ranged from puppies to adult border collies.

lead_independence.headline: Martin County deputies wore hazmat suits to remove dogs from feces-covered Palm City home
lead_independence.lead: Sheriff John Budensiek said the food bowls and water bowls inside the home were covered in feces. The dogs, which are supposed to be border collies, were covered in feces and appeared solid black instead of their normal white and black coloring. Budensiek said some of the dogs were skittish and hiding, making it difficult for investigators to remove them.

source_focus.source_lead: On July 22, Animal Services responded to another complaint alleging more than 20 dogs were inside the home, that several deceased animals may have been in the garage, that the home did not have functioning air conditioning and that the dogs had not been allowed outside since 2022, according to the report.
